reviewed_scope: Namespace identity reconciliation, direct targets and C whole-function values; all changed code hunks inspected. Native compilation/semantic claims are limited to the documented authored C++/Rust proofs.

families.native-rust: C definition and address value now refer to extensions::main; Rust body only gains qualified-name comment.
families.namespace-cpp: Definitions and direct calls bind to their original left/left::deep/right functions; true global target unchanged. All12 emitted C bodies compile/execute under GCC/ClangO0/O2.
families.dwarf-pointer: C definition/getter/main agree on left::target; all3 exact emitted bodies compile/execute with explicit address check. Rust/Go call spelling follows canonical path; their pointer output unchanged.
families.namespace-rust: Ordinary crate/module definitions and direct calls retain same-address identity. C runtime main pointer now agrees with dwarf_namespaces::main definition. Go scope paths follow recovered identity; module/package assembly is not claimed. Invalid reference/template/impl scopes are unchanged.
families.raw-namespace: Only crate main identity/comment and C runtime pointer change; raw union module target and direct wrapper are exact parent records and compile/execute in C.

limitations: No claim that translating C++ namespace functions into Go produces a type-checkable Go package. For example direct_shadow(left uint32) now spells left.target(left), which collides with the parameter in Go; parent target(left) already selected the unrelated +40 function. This is a P9 cross-language name-spelling follow-up, not a native-Go change; all native-Go captures seen are byte-identical.
Rust/Go per-function declarations encode enclosing namespaces in comments; no whole Rust-runtime or cross-language Go recompilation claim.
